newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Sept 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Sept 12.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.

Premier Li Peng, in a visit to the mainly Moslem region of Xinjiang, said religious activities must take place within limits permitted by law and urged authorities to intensify adminstration of religious activities.
A commentary said Taiwan's efforts to win a seat in the United Nations are doomed to failure and slammed the evil intentions of countries that showed a special interest in the Taiwan issue.
The Sino-British Joint Liaison Group is to meet in Beijing next week to discuss unresolved issues concerning China's resumption of sovereignty over Hong Kong.
The Tianjin commodity exchange has set rules to boost supervision and curb market risk.
Tsing Tao Brewery beer production capacity is seen reaching 750,000 tonnes a year by the end of 1997 and its per-share earning in 1996 is seen at 0.18 yuan.
An official with the Ministry of Finance says management of China's pensions is improper and urges investment in T-bills.
The Shenzhen bourse is to take new measures to improve services.
China is to speed up the drafting of a new law on non-banking financial institutions and will draw up laws on illegal transactions of banking funds in the next few years.
China has published detailed provisional regulations on the insurance industry.
An editorial cites flaws in the Bankruptcy Law and calls for a adjustments to the law.
China's cashmere production is seen at more than 10,000 tonnes in 1996 while domestic demand is seen at 6,000 to 7,000 tonnes.
